item.title: Notesy 3.7.0
item.description:
Notesy v3.7.0
Canvas notes export now.
Highlights • Export a canvas as PDF — File ▸ Export ▸ PDF… now writes a canvas instead of refusing it. The whole board goes on one page: your cards at their real positions and sizes, titles, wrapped bodies, button pills, image cards and the connecting arrows, under the note's title. Wide boards get a landscape sheet, and the page is sized to the board so the text stays vector-sharp when you zoom. • Print a canvas — File ▸ Print… prints the same sheet, scaled to fit the paper. • Export a canvas as an image — File ▸ Export ▸ Image as PNG… (previously "Drawing as PNG…") now handles canvases as well as drawings, rendering the board at 2× for a crisp picture to drop into a message or a slide. • Canvas as text — File ▸ Export ▸ Markdown… and Plain Text… turn a canvas into its cards in reading order, with each card as a heading in Markdown, so a board can be pasted into a document or an email. • The export is drawn from the stored cards rather than a screenshot, so it matches the board whether or not the canvas is open, includes cards scrolled out of view, and prints black text on white paper instead of glass on a dotted grid. • A card with an image prints the image, washed back so the text over it stays readable.
Also fixed • PDF export of an ordinary note still comes out one page; the paper size and orientation handling now accounts for landscape sheets correctly.
Requires macOS 14 or later. Unzip and move Notesy.app to Applications. Existing libraries open unchanged.

item.title: Notesy 3.6.0
item.description:
Notesy v3.6.0
Searches you can keep, a real find bar, and an outline.
Highlights • Saved searches — a search worth keeping can now be saved and re-run. They sit in a SEARCHES section of the sidebar: click one to run it, right-click to rename or remove, and the search field's menu lists them too. A saved search scopes the whole library, so it finds notes in folders you aren't looking at; picking a folder or a tag, or typing a different query, returns you to what you were doing. They are stored in the library and survive merging two libraries by name. • Search operators — the search field now understands `#tag`, `in:folder`, `is:locked`, `is:unlocked`, `has:drawing` and `is:canvas`, and mixes them with words. `in:` reaches into a folder without changing the selected one. • Find in Note (⌥⌘F) — a find strip over the page with every match highlighted, the current one in orange, and "3 of 12" as you go. ⌘G and ⇧⌘G step, and the search starts from the selected text, like every other Mac app. Find and Replace (⇧⌥⌘F) adds a replace row; Replace All is one undoable edit, so ⌘Z puts the whole note back. • Find Next/Previous — ⌘G and ⇧⌘G work even when the strip is closed, and reopen it with the last query. • Outline — View ▸ Outline (⌥⌘O) or the new toolbar button lists this note's headings, indented by level, and clicking one jumps to it. It reads what people already type: `#` heading lines, a line underlined with `===` or `---`, and short ALL-CAPS lines, which is what the built-in templates use.
Also fixed • Quick Switcher (⌘O) no longer disappears behind an open canvas. Canvas pages are created the first time you open them and were landing on top of the panel; the panel and the find bar now always stay above the page. • The Quick Switcher and the find bar paint a near-opaque reading surface, so result rows and match counts stay readable over text, ink and paper. • Find, Find and Replace, Find Next/Previous and Outline grey out for canvas, drawing and locked notes instead of beeping at them. • The find bar closes when you switch notes or the library locks, rather than highlighting the same offsets in a different note.
Requires macOS 14 or later. Unzip and move Notesy.app to Applications. Existing libraries open unchanged.

item.title: Notesy 3.5.0
item.description:
Notesy v3.5.0
Drawings you can roam, and buttons that do things.
Highlights • Scrollable, zoomable drawings — a drawing note is now a fixed page (1600×2200 for new ones) inside a real scroll view. Two-finger scroll pans, pinch or ⌘-scroll zooms from 25% to 400% around the pointer. The page stays put when you resize the window, and only the visible slice is rendered, so big pages stay light. • Buttons on notes — put a clickable button above a note's text. Each one opens a note, opens a URL, or runs an app action: New Note, New Drawing, New Canvas, Feature Canvas, Quick Switcher, Search, Next Note, Previous Note. Add one with Edit → Insert Button… (⇧⌘B), or right-click a button to run, edit or remove it. • Buttons on canvases — any canvas card can carry a button instead of a link, with the same actions. Right-click a card → Add Button…; the card's title line says what the action does and the button carries the label. • Buttons are stored, not typed — a button is data in the library, so it can't be half-typed, it survives saving and reloading, and a library written by a newer Notesy still opens (an unknown action falls back instead of failing).
Also fixed • Quick Switcher's menu shortcut reads ⌘O again, and still toggles open and closed. • Focus Mode moved to ⌘⇧F, so ⌘F is Find again. • Removed a duplicated "Copy as Rich Text" item and a doubled separator above "Empty Trash…". • Checklist boxes and [[wikilinks]] now respond where you point — clicks account for the text container's inset. • Locking a note refreshes the page immediately, and right-click → Lock on an unselected row selects it first. • Colour labels: dots draw in the note list, and right-click → Color sets red, orange, yellow, green, blue or purple. • Locked notes keep their text out of search, Spotlight, backlinks, tags and the Quick Switcher; titles stay searchable.
Requires macOS 14 or later. Unzip and move Notesy.app to Applications. Existing libraries open unchanged.

item.title: Notesy 3.3.0
item.description:
Notesy v3.3.0
Quick-switcher toggle fix and a visible Empty Trash command.
Highlights • Quick Switcher (⌘O) now toggles — press it once to open, again to close. No more stuck panels. • File → Empty Trash… is now a real menu item, so you can purge the Trash from anywhere without hunting for a toolbar button. The existing toolbar button also shows correctly when you are viewing Trash. • Emptying trash now saves immediately, so deletions survive a crash between the alert and the next save cycle.

item.title: Notesy 3.2.0
item.description:
Notesy v3.2.0
Harder to lose a note, and friendlier when a library arrives from somewhere else.
Highlights • Your edits can no longer vanish silently — if a write fails (disk full, folder missing, iCloud unavailable) the window says so and keeps saying it until a save succeeds, with a Try Again button. Quitting with an unwritten change asks first instead of dropping it. • Daily encrypted snapshots — the last 7 days of Notes.nty are kept in Application Support/Notesy/Backups, so a bad edit or a damaged file costs a day, not a library. Importing or merging takes its own backup first, and those one-offs never use up a daily slot. • Two Macs no longer fight — when iCloud leaves a second copy behind ("Notes 2.nty"), Notesy notices it at launch and offers to merge. The newer edit of a shared note wins, notes only in one copy are kept, nothing is deleted, and the old copy is archived in Backups before the merge. • Open a .nty from Finder, or drag one onto the window — an exported library merges into the open library after a confirmation that says how many notes are new. Password-protected files ask for the password, and the current library is backed up first. • Window and selection come back — size, position, the folder you were in and the note you had open are restored on launch. • ⌘S now confirms with "✓ Saved", and File → Save is disabled while a locked read-only library is open. • Drag and drop — drop images onto the window to create drawing notes, drag notes onto a folder or onto Trash. • An unchanged save is skipped — quitting without editing leaves Notes.nty byte-identical, so iCloud stops re-uploading 1.5 MB for nothing. • Protected by tests — 12 unit tests cover merging, backup rotation, iCloud copy detection, and the refuse-to-overwrite-newer-notes rule.
Also fixed: a fresh Mac could not create its first library (the encryption path asked for a key only the "no library yet" path could mint).
Requires macOS 14 or later. Unzip and move Notesy.app to Applications. Existing libraries open unchanged.

item.title: Notesy 3.1.0
item.description:
Notesy v3.1.0
One file, one shortcut, no launch hang.
Highlights • Drawings live inside Notes.nty — every save embeds the ink and preview images in the encrypted library, so your iCloud folder holds exactly one file. You can delete the old Media folder; nothing is lost. On launch the drawings are read back out of the file, and an exported library stays fully self-contained. • Save with ⌘S — File → Save writes the library immediately instead of waiting for the half-second autosave. Autosave still runs, so nothing depends on remembering to press it. • Launch no longer hangs — the app stopped asking the login keychain for its key before the window opens. A stuck approval dialog could leave Notesy "not responding" forever; the key now lives in a private, non-synced file in Application Support. The window appears in about 0.4 seconds. • A locked library can't be overwritten — if the key is ever missing, Notesy opens read-only with an inline notice and refuses to write, rather than minting a new key over your notes. • Settings fixes — "Color Theme" sits above the theme grid again, every pane lays out top-down, and the clipped descriptions and overlapping buttons in Apple Notes, Updates and Library & Backup are gone.
Requires macOS 14 or later. Unzip and move Notesy.app to Applications.

item.title: Notesy 3.0.0
item.description:
Notesy v3.0.0
Highlights • Self-updating — Check for Updates now installs the new version for you. It downloads the release, verifies it, replaces Notesy.app and relaunches, no dragging files around. • Still manual, still private — nothing checks for updates on launch or in the background. It runs when you pick Check for Updates from the app menu or press the button in Settings. • Verified updates — every release is signed with an EdDSA key, and the replacement app's own code signature is checked before it is swapped in. A tampered download is rejected. • Same Settings and menu — Check for Updates lives in the app menu and in Settings › Updates.
Everything from 2.6.0 is still here: drawing notes, sketching over text, textured paper, and the check that told you when a new version existed.
Requires macOS 14 or later. Unzip and move Notesy.app to Applications.
Added
Writing• Word count / reading time — shown right-aligned in the title band while a text note is selected ("127 words · 1 min read"). Updated live as you type.• Export / print — File → Export as Markdown…, Export as PDF…, Print… (⌘E, ⌘⇧E, ⌘P). Markdown strips only newlines; PDF prints the page with a heading + body, and for drawings prints the rendered ink.• Focus mode — View → Focus Mode (⌘F) hides sidebar, list and toolbar, leaving just the page. Activates again to restore them.• Pin/Unpin Note — Edit → Pin/Unpin Note (⌘⇧P) or right-click a row → Pin Note. Pinned notes float to the top of every list view; a small pin icon marks them in the row.Drawing• Per-tool colour memory — pen and highlighter keep their own last colour across switches, notes and relaunches (persisted in UserDefaults). Switching to a tool that had a saved colour restores it immediately.• Stroke commits save ink immediately — writing the sidecar file after each committed stroke means a crash or quit now loses at most an ongoing gesture instead of the whole session.Organisation• Trash with restore — deleting moves a note into the Trash folder (shows a count badge on the Trash row). Right-click a trash row → Restore Note, or select Trash → click Empty Trash… to delete forever.• Quick Switcher (⌘K) — opens a 520×420 search panel over the canvas. Type a title or body fragment, see filtered matches live, press Return to jump to that note, Escape to close. Also reachable from View → Quick Switcher….• Right-click context menu on list rows — Pin Note, Share Note…, Move to Trash (or Delete Forever / Restore Note when in Trash). No need to reach for toolbar buttons anymore.

item.title: Notesy 2.6.0
item.description:
Notesy 2.6.0
Check for updates, sketch on top of your notes, and put the page on real paper.
Highlights • Check for Updates — the Notesy menu now asks GitHub for the newest release and tells you whether you're current, with a Download button straight to the release page. It only runs when you ask; nothing phones home on launch. • Sketch on this note — draw directly over a text note. Ink sits on the visible page while the title band stays editable, so a margin doodle, a circled paragraph or a signature lives with the note it belongs to. • Sketch ink is part of the note — it's saved alongside the text, survives relaunch, and you can switch a note between text, sketch over text, and a full drawing note without losing the ink. • Textured paper — a new Settings › Paper switch lays the page on a photo of real paper, for typing and drawing alike. It's multiplied over the theme's own page colour, so dark themes keep dark paper and light text stays readable. Applies to drawing notes, sketch overlays and note thumbnails. • Drawing fixes — the ink surface now starts below the title band instead of under it, and the drawing palette is split into two fitted rows that scale down and stay inside the editor at every window width.
Everything from 2.5.0 is still here: the three-column glass workspace, the spatial canvas, and the nine themes.
Requires macOS 14 or later. Unzip and move Notesy.app to Applications.
